text: {"findings":[{"rule_id":"MF-005","evidence":[{"kind":"title_block","ref":"heat_treatment","page":1,"quote":"TO BE TOUGHENED UPTO 24-32 HRC."}],"comment":"The heat treatment specifies a hardness range but does not state at which manufacturing stage it applies (e.g., before or after final machining). Without this, the machinist cannot plan the process sequence, risking dimensional inaccuracy or tool damage. The designer should add the stage to the heat treatment callout.","recommended_correction":"Update the heat treatment field or note N5 to specify when toughening is to be performed relative to machining and surface treatment."},{"rule_id":"WPS-004","evidence":[{"kind":"dimension","ref":"D8","page":1,"quote":"⌀ 20"},{"kind":"note","ref":"N5","page":1,"quote":"HEAT TREATMENT :- 1) TO BE TOUGHENED UPTO 24-32 HRC. 2) RETAPPING TO BE DONE AFTER SURFACE TREATMENT AT SUPPLIER END.( IF APPLICABLE )"}],"comment":"Note N5 requires retapping after the I.Z.B.P. plating, acknowledging that threads are affected by coating buildup, yet diameter D8 carries no tolerance or allowance for the plating thickness. If D8 is a mating pin diameter, the added plating will make the finished part oversize and may prevent assembly. The designer should either assign a pre-plate undersize tolerance to D8 or explicitly state that plating thickness is excluded from the dimension.","recommended_correction":"Add a plating-compensated tolerance to D8 or a note specifying that the dimension applies before plating."}]}
